data.summary: This directory is a single scenario definition unit in an image-building (aio-config / mise) system, describing how to install the OpenAI Codex CLI into a container layer. The two files work as a pair: scenario.toml holds metadata and the version matrix consumed by `aio-config gen`, while fragment.Dockerfile holds the actual installation steps (mise aqua backend) that get resolved and injected during image assembly.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs the OpenAI Codex CLI via mise's aqua backend and verifies the binary is on PATH in both login and non-login shells. It also carries a licensing warning about redistributing the closed-source tool.
file_insights.source_summary: Declares `ARG CODEX_VERSION={{version}}` as a templated build argument, then runs `mise use -g "codex@${CODEX_VERSION}"`, `mise ls codex`, and two `bash -lc` / `bash -c` guard commands that check `command -v codex` and exit 1 with a MISSING message if the binary is absent. The file is a fragment, not a complete Dockerfile, intended to be concatenated into a larger build context.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is an L4 'app layer' build fragment in a layered image pipeline. It takes the version supplied by the generator through the CODEX_VERSION build argument, installs it globally with `mise use -g codex@${CODEX_VERSION}`, lists the installed tool, and then asserts that the `codex` executable resolves in both a login and a non-login shell so the image fails fast if installation silently broke. A comment block flags that Codex CLI is a closed-source commercial tool, so license terms must be checked before distributing images produced by `make save`.
responsibilities: Install the OpenAI Codex CLI at a pinned version using the mise aqua backend
Parameterize the installed version through the CODEX_VERSION build ARG
Verify the `codex` binary is reachable in login and non-login shells
Document the licensing risk of baking/distributing a closed-source tool

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Scenario metadata consumed by `aio-config gen` for fragment resolution, declaring the codex scenario id, category, installer and available versions. It points at fragment.Dockerfile for the actual install steps.
file_insights.source_summary: Contains a top-level comment explaining the generator contract, then key/value entries: `id = "codex"`, `name = "Codex CLI"`, a long `description`, `category = "app"`, `installer = "mise"`, and a single `[[versions]]` table with `label = "0.155.1"` and `version = "0.155.1"`. No executable code — purely declarative metadata driving fragment resolution.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML manifest registers the 'codex' scenario with the aio-config generator: a human-readable name/description, the category `app`, the installer backend `mise`, and a version table whose label/version pair (0.155.1) is substituted into the `{{version}}` placeholder in the adjacent fragment.Dockerfile. The description also records operational facts such as the install location (/opt/mise/installs) and approximate image size (~354MB), plus the same closed-source license caution found in the Dockerfile.
responsibilities: Register the codex scenario (id, name, description, category) for the generator
Declare mise as the installer backend used by the fragment
Enumerate the supported/pinned Codex CLI versions for template substitution
Record install path, size, and licensing caveats for operators
